description: Expected results for the official USGS TRIGRS tutorial (landslides-trigrs, trigrs_full/data/tutorial with the shipped tpx_in.txt + tr_in.txt, commit 9bb5ec2a): TopoIndex then serial TRIGRS, 10 x 10 grid, 2 zones, 2 rain periods, outputs at 172800 s and 216000 s. The USGS repo ships no reference outputs for the tutorial, so values are recorded from real runs of the server's engines. Three clean runs (one by hand, two through run_reference.py) gave byte-identical output grids and list file, and TrigrsLog.txt identical except the date/time lines (deterministic). Grid values are written by TRIGRS with 4 significant digits, so tolerances are set at that level.
engine_version: TRIGRS 2.1.00c (02 Feb 2022, serial trg) + TopoIndex 1.0.14 (11 May 2015); USGS git 9bb5ec2a697e161d1b602eb68ffa7acc722d5ee6

notes: Path settings changed only in the temp copies: tpx_in.txt dem/direction paths (data/... -> Data/tutorial/...) and tr_in.txt nxtfil Data/tutorial/TIdscelGrid_tutorial.asc -> .txt. The .asc name in the shipped tr_in.txt does not match the name TopoIndex writes (.txt); with it TRIGRS logs 'Skipped runoff-routing computations' and writes no runoff grids, and FS at t1 differs. With the .txt name, runoff routing runs as the tutorial intends. No physical setting was changed.
